references.text: The psalmist asks that the Lord's face shine upon him, reflecting the Aaronic blessing.
A direct allusion to the Aaronic blessing, where the people ask that God's face shine upon them.
The prayer for God to let His face shine to give salvation uses the same imagery as the blessing.
Repeated plea for God's shining face as a source of salvation and restoration.
Third repetition of the prayer for God's shining face in the same psalm.
The psalmist asks that the Lord's face shine upon his servant, with a desire for instruction in God's laws.
God's shining face brings greater joy than all earthly wealth.
God's shining face is connected to His grace and favor toward His people.
Those who walk in the light of the Lord's face are blessed.
The Lord declares that He will be gracious to whom He will be gracious, which connects to וִֽיחֻנֶּֽךָּ (and be gracious to you).
The Lord is described as light and salvation, an image reflecting God's shining face.
Paul speaks of the light from the knowledge of God's glory in the face of Jesus Christ, fulfilling the promise of God's shining face.
